Definition 7.1 (Dirichlet, Fejer, Poisson, Gauss, and Lebesgue maximal functions)
contents.reason: FR-2 does not build a torus maximal-function page. The measure-theory maximal-function backbone is already published, and this page uses the Lebesgue-point route rather than re-authoring torus maximal operators.

contents.name: Lemma 7.2 (Majorization)
contents.reason: This majorization lemma is part of Laugesen's torus-maximal-function proof of almost-everywhere summability. The batch instead cites the published Lebesgue-point theorem and keeps that stronger maximal-operator machinery out of scope.

contents.name: Theorem 7.3 (Lebesgue dominates Fejer and Poisson)
contents.reason: The domination theorem is a route to weak-(1,1) control on the torus maximal operators. FR-2 does not need that route because its a.e. statements are scaffolded through positive approximate identities and Lebesgue points.

contents.name: Corollary 7.4 (weak (1, 1) for F*, P*, and L*)
contents.reason: This weak-type theorem would duplicate maximal-function content that the library already owns on the measure page. The FR-2 design explicitly says not to duplicate the maximal-theorem route.

contents.reason: This proposition is a Dirichlet-side consequence once pointwise convergence is already known, and FR-1 already owns the Dirichlet midpoint-convergence story. FR-2 uses it only as contextual comparison, not as a new scaffold item.

contents.name: Theorem 3.4.4(a)
